facts.value: The Fitness Industry Traffic (FIT) Tracker is a new resource from the Health & Fitness Association (HFA) that provides regular updates on foot traffic to nearly 11,000 fitness facilities across the United States. Each quarter, the FIT Tracker analyzes millions of anonymized location data points to track visits to gyms and studios nationwide—providing timely, data-driven insights into consumer engagement across four key segments: High-volume low-price (HVLP) gyms Mid-priced gyms Luxury clubs Boutique/studios Developed in partnership with Sports Marketing Surveys USA (a Buffalo Groupe company) and powered by Placer.ai, the tracker offers a clear view of consumer activity at gyms and studios over time, helping industry stakeholders monitor trends, benchmark performance, and better understand how visitation patterns evolve across different price points and business models. In addition to tracking visitation by segment, the report also breaks out regional patterns, offering geographic cuts that help illustrate where activity is rising or leveling off. This added layer of insight supports benchmarking and planning at both national and local levels. The FIT Tracker is intended as a practical tool for operators, suppliers, and other industry partners looking to stay informed and make data-driven decisions.

facts.value: Garmin is reportedly working on a brand-new feature whose purpose to make the road a safer place for cyclists; evidence of the feature was found in a GC update 6 photos Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Waze might soon be getting a new alert, as Garmin, the famous maker of so many things, including smartwatches, GPS navigators , aviation and marine technology, is exploring a new way to make the road a safer place for cyclists. Garmin wants Waze drivers to be alerted whenever they are about to come across a cyclist on the road, therefore reducing the likelihood of a crash. It all starts with one of Garmin's main focuses and the horrible statistics that land every year. Garmin is investing high dollars in cycling and related technology, including smartwatch - which yes, also include bicycle tracking and statistics - and cycling computers with or without GPS. It's also making additional devices, such as dual-sensing meter pedals, radars, and lights for bicycles. Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Fatal crashes involving cyclists Unfortunately for both Garmin and everybody else, the number of fatalities involving cyclists is still at worrying levels. IIHS data shows that between 2022 and 2024, over 1,000 people were killed on the road.
